narrative: Today's ecology literature centres on how species navigate accelerating environmental change: in Conservation Biology, Australia's Black Summer bushfires offer a case study in integrating biodiversity protection into emergency response, while a companion paper in Global Ecology and Biogeography uses remote sensing to map post-fire vegetation recovery across Eastern Siberia's boreal forests. Several studies probe the limits of climate tracking: a multispecies seed-addition experiment in Ecography finds range shifts lag climate velocity at species' leading but not trailing edges, and a companion piece shows microhabitat variability can override macroclimatic predictions of range expansion. Drought emerges as a recurring driver of animal space use, reshaping both carnivore-guild interactions in Oikos and elephant habitat selection across multiple timescales in the Journal of Animal Ecology. On the evolutionary side, a seasonal epidemiological model in Ecology Letters identifies the selective forces shaping pathogen outbreak timing, while an experimental evolution study in Functional Ecology shows warming and pollinator community context jointly drive rapid floral trait divergence in Brassica rapa. In applied ecology, Conservation Biology reports that reducing livestock losses to carnivores can inadvertently reshape grazing pressure and land use, complicating coexistence strategies, and a Methods in Ecology and Evolution paper introduces a superposition method that simplifies food-web reconstruction from stable isotope data.
